answer: To resist Sybil attacks, an agent economy can bind identities to hardware enclaves via remote attestation. Before an agent begins its operational voyage, its enclave signs runtime measurements using factory-fused keys. An attacker incurs the verifiable capital cost of purchasing dedicated, certified silicon chips per identity. Nodes cross-verify attestation quotes at each epoch summit, preventing unverified clones from reaching the zenith of network influence. However, this approach centralizes trust in hardware manufacturers and cannot prevent side-channel key theft.
